description: Fix the three defects that make the oracle layer fail silently: an end-anchored mark regex that discards any criterion recording sweep evidence after the closing bracket, a named-command label that leaks into the executed shell command, and a malformed directive that is indistinguishable from a criterion with no oracle.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms exec() is stateful under the /g flag: each call resumes at lastIndex, a failed match resets lastIndex to 0, lastIndex is NOT reset when the same regex object is reused against a different string, and a zero-length-capable pattern must have lastIndex advanced manually or the iteration sticks. The page does NOT document greedy-vs-lazy backtracking under an end anchor, so no design claim in this PRD rests on fetched prose about backtracking: every parse claim here is instead pinned by a measured red/green sweep against unmodified main (see each criterion's annotation).
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: MDN's /g + exec() iteration idiom is a natural way to walk every oracle mark, but a stateful shared regex object is a re-entrancy hazard for a pure exported parser called repeatedly (parseOracleDirective); if the implementer iterates matches, the regex must be constructed per call or lastIndex explicitly reset, rather than hoisting one module-level /g regex the way the current module-level ORACLE_SUFFIX_RE (non-global, therefore stateless) is hoisted today.

userStories.notes:
Files: src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts (ORACLE_SUFFIX_RE at :94 and parseOracleDirective at :137, plus the doc comment at :86-93 that describes the end-anchor contract), test/supervisor/behavioral-gate.test.ts.

MEASURED BASELINE, do not repeat the previous plan round's false claim: main DOES support a literal ']' inside the payload. Because the end anchor forces the lazy capture to run to the FINAL ']', `parseOracleDirective("c. " + OB + "oracle: grep -qE ^v" + OB + "0-9" + CB + "+ f" + CB)` returns the whole payload "grep -qE ^v[0-9]+ f" on unmodified main (measured 2026-07-29, exit 0). Real oracle shapes in this repo depend on that: patterns.md:946 records a live `bun -e '...cs=["test $X -eq 41"]...'` oracle, and any `bun -e` payload indexing `m[1]` carries brackets too. Therefore a `[^\]]*`-style capture class is FORBIDDEN here: it would truncate that payload to "grep -qE ^v[0-9" and hand the gate a half shell command whose exit code is meaningless, i.e. it would re-introduce the exact silent-oracle class CAM-466 exists to kill. AC3 pins this explicitly.

Recommended approach (satisfies all three constraints at once, unlike any single regex): locate the LAST occurrence of the literal mark opener, then scan forward tracking bracket depth and close at the balanced ']'. Post-bracket prose is then tolerated for free (AC1), a second mark cannot be crossed (AC2), and a balanced bracket inside the payload survives (AC3). An opener that never balances yields no close: that is precisely the condition US-003 turns into the malformed kind, so keep the extraction step's failure signal separable from 'no mark present' rather than collapsing both to null.

If you do iterate matches with a /g regex instead, note the MDN row in officialDocsConsulted: a hoisted module-level /g regex is stateful across calls (lastIndex persists, and is only reset on a failed match), so construct it per call or reset lastIndex; the current ORACLE_SUFFIX_RE is safe to hoist only because it is non-global.

Patterns to grep before coding: `grep -n 'oracle' scripts/cam/patterns.md` around the falsifiability rule (patterns.md:928) and the self-nullifying-oracle bullets (patterns.md:772/:774) -- every new assertion you write must itself be swept red against unmodified main before you trust it, and never combine grep -q with -l/-L.

Gotcha specific to this PRD: its own acceptance criteria were authored to be parseable by the BROKEN parser they fix (no literal bracket in any payload, no prose after any closing bracket, brackets built via String.fromCharCode inside the test payload). Preserve that property in any criterion you touch, and do NOT write the `named-command ` label into a criterion: the label strip does not exist until US-002.

AC3 drives the real defect endpoint (the send-keys interpolation at behavioral-gate.ts:344) through an injected spawnFn, so it never touches a real tmux server: the fake returns status 0 plus a CAMGATE_0 pane so pollForExitCode returns on its first iteration (~300ms of Bun.sleepSync). Files: src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts (the OracleDirective union around :60-72, parseOracleDirective at :137, resolveNonRunnableResult at :253), test/supervisor/behavioral-gate.test.ts.

Kind boundary, so US-002 and US-003 cannot disagree: no-oracle keeps its current meaning (a mark WAS extracted but its payload is empty or is a bare kind label, e.g. the bare file-assert case at :108-111 and the bare named-command case US-002 adds). malformed is the NEW and strictly different condition: a mark opener is present but no balanced close exists, so no payload can be extracted at all -- exactly the case that returns null on main today. Do not merge the two and do not repurpose no-oracle.

Handle malformed in resolveNonRunnableResult BEFORE the `directive as NamedCommandOracle | FileAssertOracle` cast at :324, otherwise the new kind reaches the cast with an undefined .command and the gate spawns tmux for the string "undefined" and reports passed:true (measured on main by AC2's oracle: 4 tmux calls, passed:true). AC2 asserts zero tmux calls precisely to pin that ordering.

MEASURED LIVE-SURFACE FACTS behind this story's honest scope boundary, so the reviewer does not have to re-derive them: (a) `grep -rn runBehavioralGate src/` finds it only inside behavioral-gate.ts -- it has no caller inside src/; its live callers are the agent contracts, which invoke it via Bash (.claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md:89 at Layer A, .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md:50 at Layer B). (b) The reviewer contract's step 2 filters to "kind named-command or file-assert", so a malformed directive is still not re-run and still not a review-blocking finding after this story. (c) prd-oracle-lint.ts:661 does `continue` on any kind that is not named-command/file-assert, so the plan-time lint stays silent on malformed too.

The deferral is grounded in the issue's own scope clause, quoted verbatim: "NAO expandir para oracle-lint em tempo de plano, NAO mexer no tratamento de prd.json, NAO reescrever os criterios de nenhum issue ja filado." and its gotcha "Alinhar a documentacao e secundario e opcional."
